attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, endorsed.

semantics.note: A firm conditional estimate with the antecedent kept. The drafter's modality 'likely' doesn't match the words, which are an unhedged projection resting on a stated assumption. The proposition itself is faithful.

contract.note: The $33B–$48B band is an ordinary reading of 'around $40B', and the contract admits he gave no tolerance. Treating his modeling assumption as a real-world antecedent is reasonable. The early-resolution threshold of about $48B cumulative is a sensible rule.

evidence.note: The S-1 confirms H1 2026 revenue of $16,286M. Only part of the year, so it can't settle the full-year outcome.
The S-1 gives Q3 growth only as a multiple, not a full-year figure.
CNBC, citing people familiar, reports Q3 at $16.8B, about $33.1B cumulative. That is below the $48B early-resolution threshold, so it points to a higher result without settling it.

reviews.rationale: The forecast covers calendar 2026, which ends after the evaluation date. Cumulative revenue through September (about $33.1B) doesn't meet the early-resolution rule. The run-rate points above $40B, but that is a projection. The OpenAI-growth antecedent was also not checked. Not scored yet.

attribution.note: His own claim, framed as his conclusion after quoting Morgan Stanley via the FT.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense claim ('In reality, at least half'). It also carries an implied forward element, since the chips will sit idle for years. Broadcom is correctly included. 'Those chip sales' leaves the scope ambiguous.

contract.note: Reading the claim as 2026 sales, with 'years' meaning more than a year, follows the context and is ordinary. The contract rightly notes that lags for 2026 sales can't be fully seen until 2027–2028.

evidence.note: Amazon stages NVIDIA racks before power is ready. One buyer only, with no share of sales and no length of delay, so it doesn't establish 'at least half' or 'years'.
CoreWeave's install lag was weeks to months in 2025. That is a different period and one buyer, so it is context, not a contradiction of the 2026 claim.
Says the waiting time for warehoused hardware is still unknown.

reviews.rationale: No source matches 2026 NVIDIA or Broadcom sales to install dates. The Amazon reporting shows some hardware arrives before power but gives no share or duration. The CoreWeave data is from 2025 and covers one firm. The evidence doesn't settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: His own estimate in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'it appears', but the drafter's modality 'is' leaves out the hedge. The $200B–$300B figure is offered as an appearance, a graded-confidence estimate rather than a firm assertion.

contract.note: Not scoring the hedged range is fair. 'Questionable' actually qualifies the Blackwell-availability clause, not the dollar figure, but 'it appears' alone is enough to hedge the figure.

evidence.note: An analyst opinion column that disputes the figure. Commentary, not a measurement of idle chips.
Amazon holds billions per month of racks before power is ready. One buyer, far smaller than the claimed range.
Epoch models deployment with assumed lags, which confirms there is no direct public measure.

reviews.rationale: He frames the $200B–$300B idle figure as what 'appears' to be the case, a hedged estimate. Under policy it isn't scored. In any case, no public measure of uninstalled NVIDIA hardware exists. The evidence is recorded as context only.

attribution.note: His own assertions in his own post.

semantics.note: The three factual parts are kept. The clause about capacity being 'immediately sold' to the two labs is dropped and goes untested. That is a minor omission.

contract.note: Reading 'fed' as committed equity is generous to him. On a cash basis, part (b) would fall short because $35B of Amazon's commitment is conditional. Reading 'vast majority' as roughly two-thirds or more is ordinary.

evidence.note: OpenAI's $122B committed round, closed 2026-03-31, falls inside the window.
Anthropic's $30B Series G is inside the window. A company disclosure of its own funding. Led by GIC and Coatue, not the four named firms.
The $65B Series H brings the total to $122B + $30B + $65B = $217B.
A derived upper bound: at most about $119B of $217B (about 55%) came from the four firms. Its dates are those of the latest input (Series H). The inputs match e1, e5 and e6.
Caps hyperscaler money in Series H at $15B.
Caps Microsoft and NVIDIA's combined Anthropic commitment at $15B.
Puts the two labs at 15–20% of operational compute at end-2025. That is a different metric and period from the post's share of revenue and demand, so it doesn't settle part (a).

reviews.rationale: Part (b) holds: announced committed funding in the window totals $217B. Part (c) fails: at most about 55% came from Google, Amazon, Microsoft and NVIDIA, which is not a vast majority. Part (a), the 70–80% share, is unresolved because there is no measure for the right period and metric.
